title: Base change of augmented relative Cech complexes on fibred groupoids
statement: Fix the universes and small-skeleton convention of [def-weil-size-convention] and a scheme $S$ [def-pc-scheme]. Categories fibred in groupoids, their morphisms, 2-isomorphisms and 2-fibre products have the meanings of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Give each such category its big etale site: objects and arrows are those of the fibred category and coverings lie over jointly surjective etale families of schemes [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Abelian sheaves mean abelian-group-valued contravariant functors satisfying the covering equalizer condition [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Pullback $e^{-1}$ is precomposition. For $v:\mathcal V\to\mathcal X$ and an abelian sheaf $N$ on $\mathcal V$, put $(v_*N)(x)=\Gamma(\mathcal V\times_{\mathcal X}T,N|_{\mathcal V\times_{\mathcal X}T})$ for $x$ over $T$, where $\Gamma$ is the group of compatible families over all objects and restriction is precomposition with the projection. For $f:\mathcal U\to\mathcal X$ and an abelian sheaf $F$ on $\mathcal X$, let $\mathcal U_p$ be the $(p+1)$-fold 2-fibre product over $\mathcal X$ with projection $f_p$. Write $E^{-1}(f,F)=F$ and $E^p(f,F)=(f_p)_*f_p^{-1}F$ for $p\geq0$, with zero terms below degree $-1$, augmentation restriction and differential $d^p=\sum_{j=0}^{p+1}(-1)^jd_j^*$, where $d_j$ omits the $j$-th factor. Let $e:\mathcal Y\to\mathcal X$, let $\mathcal V=\mathcal Y\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal U$ with projection $g:\mathcal V\to\mathcal Y$, and use the base-changed nerve for $E^\bullet(g,e^{-1}F)$. There is a canonical natural isomorphism of augmented complexes of abelian sheaves $e^{-1}E^\bullet(f,F)\cong E^\bullet(g,e^{-1}F)$, whose degree $-1$ component is the identity on $e^{-1}F$. It respects the augmentation and every face pullback and is natural in $F$. In particular it induces the canonical isomorphism between these complexes in the ordinary derived category of abelian sheaves. No algebraicity or representability hypothesis is needed.

source.place: Tag 06XC (lemma-base-change-cech-complex), with the etale topology; the augmented-complex formulation includes the degree -1 identity.

proof.text: Every functor $w:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ over $\mathit{Sch}/S$ between categories fibred in groupoids preserves cartesian arrows, since all arrows are cartesian; so by [lem-sfb-fibred-site-functor-continuity], with base the big etale site of $S$-schemes, $w$ is continuous and cocontinuous for the big etale topologies. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-cocontinuous-topos-adjunction] shows that precomposition $w^{-1}$ and the compatible-family functor $R$, indexed by pairs $(a,\psi:w(a)\to z)$, send sheaves of sets to sheaves of sets. For $z$ over $T$, sending $(t:T'\to T,a,\phi:w(a)\cong t^*z)$ to $(a,\text{(cartesian arrow }t^*z\to z)\circ\phi)$ is an equivalence from $(\mathit{Sch}/T)\times_{z,\mathcal B}\mathcal A$ onto these pairs (an arrow $w(a)\to z$ factors uniquely through the cartesian lift), so compatible families correspond and $(w_*N)(z)=R N(z)$, compatibly with restrictions (Tag 06W6). Both formulas commute with the forgetful functor to sets, and an abelian presheaf is a sheaf when its underlying presheaf of sets is [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Thus all terms of $E$ are abelian sheaves and all maps are sheaf morphisms. In a shared-target model a nerve object is $(u_0,\ldots,u_p,x;\gamma_i:f(u_i)\cong x)$. Faces delete coordinates. Deleting positions $i<j$ in either order gives the same tuple, so the two occurrences in $d^{p+1}d^p$ have signs $(-1)^{i+j}$ and $(-1)^{i+j-1}$ and cancel; the two restrictions of the augmentation also agree.

source.place: Tag 06XC (lemma-base-change-cech-complex); Tag 06TS (lemma-functoriality-sheaves) via stacks.tex Tag 06NW; Tag 06W6 (equation-pushforward).

proof.text: Write $v_i=(y_i,u_i,\alpha_i:f(u_i)\cong e(y_i))$. An object of $\mathcal V_p$ is $(v_i,y;\beta_i:y_i\cong y)$. The functor $h_p$ sends it to $(u_i,e(y);e(\beta_i)\alpha_i)$ in $\mathcal U_p$, on arrows componentwise. The corresponding functor to $\mathcal Y\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal U_p$ is an equivalence: an object $(y,(u_i,x;\gamma_i),\delta:x\cong e(y))$ is sent back to the tuple with $v_i=(y,u_i,\delta\gamma_i)$ and all $\beta_i=1$. Composing in either order is naturally isomorphic to the identity, with components $\beta_i$ on the first side and $\delta$ on the second. The arrow relation in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids] verifies these isomorphisms componentwise. Hence the square with sides $g_p,f_p,e,h_p$ is $2$-cartesian and $f_ph_p=e g_p$ in this model. Deleting a coordinate commutes with $h_p$.

source.place: Tag 06XC, test-fibre comparison; lemma-generalities, displayed tuple formula.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-fibred-presheaf-pushforward-base-change] to this square and $N=f_p^{-1}F$. Since $h_p^{-1}f_p^{-1}F=g_p^{-1}e^{-1}F$ by precomposition, it gives an isomorphism $\beta^p:e^{-1}(f_p)_*f_p^{-1}F\to(g_p)_*g_p^{-1}e^{-1}F$ for every $p\geq0$. Its component at $y/T$ restricts a compatible family along the test-fibre functor induced by $h_p$. It is natural in $F$ and in arrows of $y$. Both sides are sheaves by step 1, so it is an isomorphism of sheaves.

For a face $d_j$, restrict a compatible family $s$ and evaluate at a test object $z$ of the degree-$(p+1)$ fibre. The two composites, first face then $\beta$ or first $\beta$ then face, have respective values $s_{d_jh_{p+1}(z)}$ and $s_{h_pd_j(z)}$, including the coefficient restrictions. They agree by the coordinate formula of step 2. The restriction description in [lem-sfb-fibred-presheaf-pushforward-base-change] therefore gives $\beta^{p+1}e^{-1}(d_j^*)=d_j^*\beta^p$. Set $\beta^{-1}=1_{e^{-1}F}$. For $t\in F(e(y))$, both augmented composites at $z$ are the restriction of $t$ along the structural arrow to $e(y)$; hence augmentation commutes as well.

source.place: Tag 06XC, canonical comparison; lemma-generalities-sheafified and remark-cech-complex-presheaves.

proof.text: Add the face equalities with signs $(-1)^j$; precomposition is additive sectionwise. Together with the augmentation equality and the unique maps between zero terms below $-1$, the $\beta^p$ define a natural isomorphism of augmented complexes. Their inverses commute with the differentials by composing the same equalities with the termwise inverses. Applying the localization functor $Q$ of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] to this complex isomorphism and its inverse gives the claimed canonical isomorphism in the ordinary derived category. Only fibred-groupoid data and big-etale sheaf functoriality were used.

source.place: Tag 06XC, augmented formulation; derived consequence from localization definition 05RU.
